observations.content:
# Proposal: Engram Gemini/Codex Parity

## Intent

Alinear `gentle-ai` con el contrato real de `work/engram` para que Gemini CLI y Codex reciban la misma inyeccion MCP/memory protocol que hoy espera el ecosistema.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Agregar `--tools=agent` a overlays/config MCP de Claude, Gemini, OpenCode y VS Code en `internal/components/engram/inject.go`.
- Habilitar soporte real de Codex via `~/.codex/config.toml`, incluyendo bloque `[mcp_servers.engram]` e instruction files `engram-instructions.md` y `engram-compact-prompt.md`.
- Extender el modelo/adapter para soportar estrategia TOML e incorporar tests unitarios y E2E de Gemini/Codex/idempotencia.
- Evaluar cleanup de `GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD` solo si puede hacerse sin invadir el flujo actual.

### Out of Scope
- Cambiar `internal/agents/gemini/adapter.go` para escribir `system.md`; no es delta real frente a `engram`.
- Rediseñar el pipeline SDD/persona o agregar un parser TOML general-purpose.
- Soportar contratos legacy de `engram` sin `--tools=agent` mas alla de documentar version minima.

## Approach

Implementar primero la paridad MCP de bajo riesgo, luego encapsular soporte Codex TOML con helpers string-based portados de `engram`, manteniendo el patron actual de injection/idempotencia y cubriendolo con pruebas de archivo reales.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `internal/components/engram/inject.go` | Modified | overlays MCP, branching Codex, instruction files |
| `internal/agents/codex/adapter.go` | Modified | `SupportsMCP`, `MCPConfigPath`, estrategia/config path real |
| `internal/model/types.go` | Modified | nueva estrategia MCP para TOML |
| `internal/components/engram/inject_test.go` | Modified | asserts `--tools=agent`, Gemini/Codex/idempotencia |
| `internal/agents/codex/adapter_test.go` | Modified | capacidades y paths TOML |
| `e2e/e2e_test.sh` | Modified | escenarios Gemini/Codex de instalacion real |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Upsert TOML fragil sobre configs complejas | Med | portar helpers probados de `engram` sin ampliar scope |
| `experimental_compact_prompt_file` cambie en Codex | Med | aislar soporte como best-effort y cubrir con tests |
| Usuarios con `engram` viejo fallen por `--tools=agent` | Med | documentar version minima y verificar mensajes de error |

## Rollback Plan

Revertir la nueva estrategia TOML y restaurar overlays JSON previos; como la inyeccion es localizada a archivos de config, basta eliminar bloques/archivos `engram-*` y volver a los defaults anteriores.

## Dependencies

- Contrato fuente: `work/engram/internal/setup/setup.go`
- Version de `engram` que soporte `mcp --tools=agent`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Gemini/Claude/OpenCode/VS Code escriben MCP con `--tools=agent`.
- [ ] Codex instala `~/.codex/config.toml` + instruction files sin duplicados tras dos corridas.
- [ ] Tests unitarios cubren Gemini/Codex/idempotencia y pasan con el nuevo contrato.
- [ ] E2E valida archivos reales de Gemini y Codex para el componente `engram`.

observations.title: sdd/engram-gemini-codex-parity/design
observations.content:
# Design: engram-gemini-codex-parity

## Technical Approach

Align gentle-ai's engram injection with the real engram contract from `work/engram/internal/setup/setup.go`. Three workstreams: (A) fix `--tools=agent` flag across all JSON overlays, (B) enable Codex MCP via new `StrategyTOMLFile` + instruction files, (C) add Gemini env cleanup. Each is self-contained; A is prerequisite to B/C. The approach reuses engram's string-based TOML helpers verbatim (no TOML library) and follows existing adapter/strategy patterns.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: New MCPStrategy vs hook in Inject()

**Choice**: Add `StrategyTOMLFile` (new `MCPStrategy` constant = 3) to `model/types.go` and handle it as a new `case` in `engram/inject.go`.
**Alternatives**: (1) Handle TOML inside the existing `StrategyMergeIntoSettings` branch with an agent-specific `if`; (2) Add a Codex-specific hook method to the Adapter interface.
**Rationale**: A new strategy is the cleanest. The current pattern dispatches on `MCPStrategy()` — adding a TOML case is consistent with how `StrategyMCPConfigFile` was added for Cursor/VSCode. An adapter-specific hook breaks the abstraction. An `if` inside `StrategyMergeIntoSettings` conflates JSON merge with TOML upsert.

### Decision: Port TOML helpers from engram vs add BurntSushi/toml

**Choice**: Copy `upsertCodexEngramBlock()` and `upsertTopLevelTOMLString()` from `engram/internal/setup/setup.go` into a new file `internal/components/filemerge/toml.go`.
**Alternatives**: (1) Import `BurntSushi/toml` for full parsing; (2) Keep TOML helpers inside `engram/inject.go`.
**Rationale**: Engram's string-based approach is battle-tested for the limited TOML subset Codex uses. Adding a real TOML parser brings a dependency for 2 functions. Placing in `filemerge/` keeps the pattern consistent — JSON merge is already there.

### Decision: Codex instruction files — where to write

**Choice**: Write `engram-instructions.md` and `engram-compact-prompt.md` inside `engram/inject.go`'s Inject() function, after the MCP config block, gated on `adapter.Agent() == model.AgentCodex`.
**Alternatives**: (1) Add new Adapter interface methods like `InstructionFiles()`; (2) Handle in `setup.go`/`run.go`.
**Rationale**: These files are engram-specific, not a general adapter concern. The `Inject()` function already handles both MCP config AND system prompt for other agents. Instruction files are the Codex equivalent of system prompt injection — same function, different mechanism.

### Decision: Instruction file content source

**Choice**: Embed `memoryProtocolMarkdown` and `codexCompactPromptMarkdown` as new files in `internal/assets/codex/` (parallel to `internal/assets/claude/engram-protocol.md`), loaded via `assets.MustRead()`.
**Alternatives**: (1) Inline as Go string constants in inject.go; (2) Share the existing `claude/engram-protocol.md`.
**Rationale**: `claude/engram-protocol.md` has diverged from engram's `memoryProtocolMarkdown` (gentle-ai has added proactive-save triggers, topic update rules that don't exist in engram's version). For Codex, we want engram's exact content since `engram setup codex` already writes it. Using `assets/codex/` keeps per-agent content organized and testable via golden files.

### Decision: `--tools=agent` flag — update overlays vs. dynamic construction

**Choice**: Update the 4 hardcoded JSON byte slices in `inject.go` to include `"--tools=agent"` in the args array.
**Alternatives**: Build overlay JSON dynamically at runtime.
**Rationale**: The overlays are already static `[]byte` vars. Changing the literal strings is the minimum-risk fix. Dynamic construction adds complexity for zero benefit.

## Data Flow

### Engram injection for Codex (new):

```
run.go: componentApplyStep.Run()
  └─ engram.Inject(home, codexAdapter)
       ├─ adapter.SupportsMCP() → true (changed)
       ├─ adapter.MCPStrategy() → StrategyTOMLFile (new)
       │   └─ adapter.MCPConfigPath(home, "engram") → ~/.codex/config.toml
       │       └─ filemerge.UpsertCodexEngramBlock(existing) → updated TOML
       │           └─ filemerge.WriteFileAtomic(path, updated)
       ├─ adapter.Agent() == AgentCodex → write instruction files
       │   ├─ assets.MustRead("codex/engram-instructions.md") → ~/.codex/engram-instructions.md
       │   ├─ assets.MustRead("codex/engram-compact-prompt.md") → ~/.codex/engram-compact-prompt.md
       │   └─ filemerge.UpsertTopLevelTOMLString(content, key, path) for:
       │       ├─ model_instructions_file = "~/.codex/engram-instructions.md"
       │       └─ experimental_compact_prompt_file = "~/.codex/engram-compact-prompt.md"
       └─ adapter.SupportsSystemPrompt() → true (existing, writes agents.md)
```

### componentPaths for Codex (new case):

```
componentPaths(home, selection, adapters, ComponentEngram)

| 1 | `TestUpsertCodexEngramBlock_Empty` | `filemerge/toml_test.go` | Empty input → produces `[mcp_servers.engram]\ncommand = "engram"\nargs = ["mcp", "--tools=agent"]` |

| 12 | `TestInjectCodexInjectsTOMLKeys` (new) | `engram/inject_test.go` | config.toml has `model_instructions_file` + `experimental_compact_prompt_file` |
| 13 | `TestInjectCodexIsIdempotent` (new) | `engram/inject_test.go` | Inject x2 → no duplicates in TOML, changed=false on second |
| 14 | `TestInjectGeminiToolsFlagPresent` (new) | `engram/inject_test.go` | settings.json args has `--tools=agent` |

**Wave 4 — E2E (Tier 2, `RUN_FULL_E2E=1`):**

## Migration / Rollout

No data migration. Changes are purely additive:
- Users with existing Codex installs get MCP support on next `gentle-ai install`
- Users with existing Gemini/Claude/OpenCode/VSCode installs get `--tools=agent` added to their config on next run (JSON merge is additive, won't break existing)

**Minimum engram version**: >= v1.8.x (when `--tools=agent` was standardized). Document in release notes.

observations.title: Idempotency fix: TOML single-pass mutation for Codex
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed non-idempotency in Codex TOML injection by composing all TOML mutations (UpsertCodexEngramBlock + UpsertTopLevelTOMLString x2) in a single pass before the atomic write.

**Why**: Original approach did three sequential read-mutate-write cycles. On the second run, UpsertCodexEngramBlock would produce a slightly different string (extra blank line normalization) from the intermediate state, causing WriteFileAtomic to detect a diff and report changed=true.

**Where**: internal/components/engram/inject.go — StrategyTOMLFile case

**Learned**: All TOML helpers are idempotent in isolation, but sequencing intermediate writes breaks idempotency. Always compose mutations before the final write. The fix was to: (1) determine instruction paths, (2) read existing content once, (3) apply all 3 upserts in sequence, (4) write once atomically.

observations.title: Fixed CI regression: SDD single-mode post-check and stale goldens after ee66b01
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed 4 categories of CI failures introduced or exposed by commit ee66b01 (feat: add codex and engram parity).

**Why**: CI was red on main after ee66b01. Four distinct root causes needed fixes.

**Where**:
- `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` — post-check guard
- `internal/cli/run_component_paths_test.go` — test name + assertion
- `internal/components/permissions/inject_test.go` — deny-list assertion value
- `testdata/golden/engram-claude-mcp.golden` — stale golden
- `testdata/golden/engram-opencode-settings.golden` — stale golden

**Learned**:

1. **Regression (6745dbf)**: SDD post-check for `sdd-apply` was made unconditional in `inject.go:213`. Single-mode overlay (`sdd-overlay-single.json`) only has `sdd-orchestrator`, never `sdd-apply`. Fixed by restoring `if sddMode == model.SDDModeMulti &&` guard. The 6745dbf commit intentionally broadened the check but that was wrong for single mode.

2. **Preexisting test mismatch (ee73ea4)**: The commit changed plugin install from multi-only to all SDD modes AND renamed the test in `inject_test.go`, but failed to update the parallel CLI test `TestComponentPathsSDDSingleExcludesOpenCodePlugin` in `run_component_paths_test.go`. Renamed to `TestComponentPathsSDDSingleIncludesOpenCodePlugin` and flipped the assertion.

3. **Test authored with wrong expectation (ee66b01 + d65c4cc)**: `TestInjectAddsEnvToDenyList` was checking for plain `".env"` in the Claude Code deny list, but commit d65c4cc changed the format to `"Read(.env)"` / `"Edit(.env)"`. Test was searching for the pre-fix value. Fixed to check for `"Read(.env)"`.

4. **Stale goldens (ee66b01)**: The commit added `--tools=agent` to engram MCP args but didn't update the two golden files. Updated both goldens to include `--tools=agent` in the command args.

observations.title: Bugfix: AgentCodex missing from catalog — E2E config.toml not created
observations.content:
**What**: Added `AgentCodex` to `catalog.AllAgents()` slice in `internal/catalog/agents.go`. Also fixed `cleanup_test_env()` in `e2e/lib.sh` to remove `~/.codex` and `~/.gemini`. Updated two unit tests that hardcoded the agent count.

**Why**: The Codex adapter, inject logic (`StrategyTOMLFile`), and TOML helpers were fully implemented, but `catalog.IsSupportedAgent("codex")` returned `false` because Codex was never added to `allAgents`. The planner resolver puts unrecognized agents in `UnsupportedAgents` (not `resolved.Agents`). The runtime iterates only `resolved.Agents` to call `engram.Inject()`, so Codex was silently skipped — no config.toml was ever written, E2E failed.

**Where**: 
- `internal/catalog/agents.go` — added `{ID: model.AgentCodex, Name: "Codex", Tier: model.TierFull, ConfigPath: "~/.codex"}` to `allAgents`
- `e2e/lib.sh` — added `rm -rf "$HOME/.codex"` and `rm -rf "$HOME/.gemini"` to `cleanup_test_env()`
- `internal/cli/install_test.go` — updated `TestNormalizeInstallFlagsDefaults` to include `model.AgentCodex` in expected agents list
- `internal/tui/model_test.go` — replaced hardcoded `screensAgentOptions()` with `screens.AgentOptions()` so the helper stays in sync with the catalog

**Learned**: When adding a new agent, the catalog is the single gate — adapter, inject, factory, and engram setup can all be wired correctly, but if `catalog.IsSupportedAgent()` returns false, the resolver silently treats the agent as unsupported and the entire inject chain is bypassed. Always add to `allAgents` as part of the new-agent checklist.

observations.title: Fixed Codex CLI catalog wiring for end-to-end installs
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed the remaining E2E failure by adding `AgentCodex` to the supported agent catalog so CLI/planner resolution actually runs Codex installs, and updated related cleanup/test expectations.
**Why**: CI E2E failed because `install --agent codex --component engram` treated Codex as unsupported, so `~/.codex/config.toml` was never created even though unit-level inject logic was correct.
**Where**: `internal/catalog/agents.go`, `e2e/lib.sh`, `internal/cli/install_test.go`, `internal/tui/model_test.go`.
**Learned**: Adding a new adapter is not enough in this repo; the catalog is part of the runtime contract used by planner/CLI resolution, so missing catalog registration can hide behind passing unit tests and only surface in E2E.

observations.content:
## Goal
Investigar por que el one-liner de PowerShell de Gentle AI deja usuarios sin la version nueva y sin el comando `upgrade`.

## Instructions
- Verificar el problema antes de afirmarlo.
- No hacer cambios todavia; primero diagnosticar la causa.

## Discoveries
- `scripts/install.ps1` consulta correctamente `releases/latest` del repo `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`; no hay version hardcodeada.
- El instalador copia el binario a `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gentle-ai\bin`, pero si ese path no domina el PATH del usuario, puede seguir ejecutandose otro `gentle-ai.exe` mas viejo.
- La verificacion actual usa `gentle-ai version` en lugar del binario exacto recien instalado, asi que puede dar un falso positivo.
- `internal/app/app.go` si registra el comando `upgrade`, por lo que el error `unknown command "upgrade"` apunta a un binario viejo en PATH.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Inspeccione el flujo del instalador PowerShell y descarte que descargue una version hardcodeada.
- ✅ Corrobore que el comando `upgrade` existe en la CLI actual.
- ✅ Aisle la causa mas probable como PATH shadowing de un binario viejo.

## Next Steps
- Actualizar `scripts/install.ps1` para verificar `& $destPath version` y detectar conflictos con `Get-Command gentle-ai -All`.
- Opcionalmente ofrecer agregar/prepender `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gentle-ai\bin` al User PATH automaticamente.

## Relevant Files
- `scripts/install.ps1` — flujo de instalacion, descarga y verificacion del binario.
- `internal/app/app.go` — registro del comando `upgrade`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — publicacion de releases por tags.

observations.content:
**What**: Validated the real installer update flow for `engram` using `go run ./cmd/gentle-ai update` and `go run ./cmd/gentle-ai upgrade --dry-run engram`. observations.title: Hardened update-check failure handling
observations.content:
**What**: Preserved remote release lookup failures as `CheckFailed`, rendered incomplete-check summaries instead of success messaging, and made `update`/`upgrade` return errors when update checks fail.
**Why**: Update checks were degrading fetch failures into success-like states and some CLI paths could claim everything was up to date even when GitHub lookups failed.
**Where**: internal/update/check.go, internal/update/render.go, internal/app/app.go, internal/update/render_test.go, internal/app/update_test.go
**Learned**: The `upgrade` report renderer assumes a fully successful check pass; the safest minimal fix was to surface the check report and stop before rendering upgrade success messaging when checks are incomplete.

- ✅ Added targeted regression coverage in `internal/update/check_test.go`, `internal/update/render_test.go`, `internal/update/upgrade/executor_test.go`, `internal/app/update_test.go`, and adjusted `internal/app/upgrade_test.go` expectations.

observations.title: Fixed hardcoded models overwriting user opencode.json config
observations.content:
**What**: Removed hardcoded `"model"` fields from `sdd-overlay-multi.json` and simplified `injectModelAssignments()` to only write models when explicitly chosen via the TUI model picker.
**Why**: Users reported that re-running the installer with SDD multi-mode was overwriting their model choices with hardcoded `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-6` values. The deep merge in `MergeJSONObjects` always let the overlay win over the user's existing config.
**Where**: `internal/assets/opencode/sdd-overlay-multi.json`, `internal/components/sdd/inject.go`, `internal/components/sdd/inject_test.go`, `e2e/e2e_test.sh`, `testdata/golden/sdd-opencode-multi-settings.golden`
**Learned**: The working version (`979d420`) had NO model fields in the overlay. Commits `acd26a2` and `dc03cb8` introduced the regression by adding model fields to the overlay and a `rootModelID` fallback that propagated to all sub-agents. The fix restores the original design: overlay defines agent structure only, models come exclusively from explicit user choice.

observations.title: OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance - exploration findings
observations.content:
**What**: Investigated the OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance problem and the current state of the fix.

**Why**: Understanding whether the current fix (bd73beb) is correct or whether more work is needed to break OpenCode's runtime model inheritance without overwriting user config.

**Where**: internal/components/sdd/inject.go, internal/assets/opencode/sdd-overlay-multi.json, internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go

**Learned**:
1. OpenCode docs EXPLICITLY confirm: "If you don't specify a model, primary agents use the model globally configured while subagents will use the model of the primary agent that invoked the subagent." This confirms the inheritance behavior is real.

2. Current state (bd73beb): Overlay has NO model fields. Models are only injected when user explicitly picks them via TUI. This means: fresh install → no model fields → subagents inherit from orchestrator runtime model (the problem we tried to fix in acd26a2).

3. The acd26a2 approach tried to propagate rootModelID to ALL sub-agents (both as fallback AND as explicit), but the deep merge let that overwrite user's EXISTING agent configs.

4. The real fix needs SELECTIVE behavior:
   - If user already has a "model" field on sdd-init in their opencode.json → don't overwrite it
   - If user does NOT have "model" on sdd-init → inject a default (rootModel or a hardcoded default like "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6")
   - TUI explicit assignment always wins regardless

5. The mergeObjects function in json_merge.go does a deep merge where overlays win on scalar conflict (line 197: result[key] = overlayValue). So if the overlay has "model": "anthropic/..." and the user already has "model": "openai/gpt-4" in their opencode.json agent, the OVERLAY WINS. That's the bug.

6. Current fix (bd73beb) resolves the overwrite problem but leaves the inheritance problem unresolved — fresh installs with no TUI model choice get sub-agents with no model, and OpenCode will inherit the parent's runtime model.

7. Key insight: The CORRECT fix for the pre-merge check approach needs to be in injectModelAssignments or the call site — read the existing opencode.json BEFORE building the overlay, then only add model fields for agents that don't already exist in the user's config (or have no existing model field).

8. User's actual opencode.json has model fields on all sdd-* agents (sdd-apply: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, sdd-design: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6, etc.) set from the TUI. The bd73beb fix correctly preserves these.

observations.title: Fixed OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance with 3-way logic
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented 3-way model injection logic in `injectModelAssignments` to correctly handle OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance without overwriting user config.

**Why**: Sub-agents with no explicit `"model"` field inherit the orchestrator's model at runtime (OpenCode behavior). Previous fix hardcoded models in the overlay JSON, which caused re-installs to overwrite user model choices via deep merge.

**Where**: 
- `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` — restored `readOpenCodeRootModel()`, added `readExistingAgentModels()`, updated `injectModelAssignments()` signature and logic, updated call site in `Inject()`
- `internal/components/sdd/inject_test.go` — updated 2 tests, added 2 new tests, fixed unit test call signature

**Learned**: 
- Decision tree: (1) TUI assignment wins, (2) agent KEY already in user config → skip (don't inject even without model field), (3) new agent + rootModel exists → inject rootModel
- Rule 2 catches the intentional-no-model case: if user defined the agent without a model field, `existingAgentKeys[phase]` is true and we skip — the merge will preserve the user's no-model state
- Golden test for multi-mode stays unchanged because the golden is a fresh install (no pre-existing config) → no root model → no model fields
- The `readExistingAgentModels` function reads BEFORE the merge, so it sees only the user's original config keys (not the overlay's agents)

observations.title: Fixed OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance with 3-way logic
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented 3-way model injection logic in `injectModelAssignments` to correctly handle the OpenCode sub-agent model inheritance problem without overwriting user config.
**Why**: OpenCode documents that sub-agents inherit the model of their invoking agent at runtime if they have no explicit "model" field. The previous fix (bd73beb) removed hardcoded models from the overlay, which broke inheritance again. The fix before THAT (acd26a2) hardcoded models which overwrote user config on reinstall.
**Where**: `internal/components/sdd/inject.go`, `internal/components/sdd/inject_test.go`
**Learned**: The 3-way decision logic: (1) TUI explicit assignment always wins, (2) if the agent key already exists in user's opencode.json → skip entirely (preserve whatever they have, including no-model), (3) if the agent is new AND rootModelID exists → inject rootModelID as default. This satisfies: fresh install breaks inheritance, reinstall preserves user choices, TUI always wins. Key: added `readExistingAgentModels()` to detect which agent keys already exist in user config (not just which have model fields). Added `readOpenCodeRootModel()` back. Commit: f38d5ff.

observations.title: Exploration: sync sdd-orchestrator model to gentleman agent
observations.content:
**What**: Exploration of where and how to sync the sdd-orchestrator model assignment to the gentleman agent in OpenCode config.

**Why**: Both `gentleman` (mode: primary, from persona inject.go openCodeAgentOverlayJSON) and `sdd-orchestrator` (mode: primary, from sdd-overlay-multi/single.json) are primary conductors. The TUI model picker assigns a model to `sdd-orchestrator` but `gentleman` always inherits from runtime — wrong behavior.

**Where**: 
- internal/components/sdd/inject.go — injectModelAssignments() at line 748
- internal/components/persona/inject.go — openCodeAgentOverlayJSON (no model field)
- internal/assets/opencode/sdd-overlay-multi.json — no gentleman key
- internal/assets/opencode/sdd-overlay-single.json — no gentleman key
- internal/model/selection.go — ModelAssignments map[string]ModelAssignment
- internal/model/model_assignment.go — ModelAssignment struct

**Learned**: 
- injectModelAssignments() iterates over agents already in the OVERLAY, not the full opencode.json
- The overlay only has sdd-* agents; gentleman is NOT in the sdd overlays
- The persona overlay (openCodeAgentOverlayJSON) defines gentleman with NO model field
- injectModelAssignments() is called ONLY in multi mode (sddMode == SDDModeMulti)
- The cleanest fix is Option D: in injectModelAssignments(), after processing all phases, if assignments["sdd-orchestrator"] is set, also inject the same model into agents["gentleman"] if that key exists in the overlay map (which requires adding gentleman to sdd-overlay-multi.json and sdd-overlay-single.json without defining it fully — OR just handling it as a special case outside the loop)
- Best approach: Option D — duplicate assignment to gentleman BEFORE the loop, or add a post-loop special case. No need to touch the persona overlay.
- Risk: if gentleman is added to the SDD overlay JSONs, the deep merge could conflict with the persona overlay that already defines gentleman's full config. The safest path is to inject only the model field programmatically (not via the JSON files).

observations.title: Run brew update before brew upgrade in self-update to fix stale cache
observations.content:
**What**: Added `brew update` call before `brew upgrade <toolName>` in the self-update flow to refresh the local formula cache before attempting an upgrade.

**Why**: Without `brew update`, Homebrew uses its local (potentially stale) formula cache. If the cache is old, it doesn't know about a new version → `brew upgrade` reports "already up to date" → binary stays old → on next launch, the update check hits GitHub, sees the new version again → infinite loop of "update available" with no actual upgrade.

**Where**: `internal/update/upgrade/strategy.go` — `brewUpgrade()` function; `internal/update/upgrade/strategy_test.go` — two new tests added.

**Learned**: The failure of `brew update` is intentionally non-fatal — if there's no network, the upgrade is still attempted with the existing cache. Pattern: run `updateCmd.Run()` and ignore the error with `_ =`, then proceed with `upgradeCmd`. The `execCommand` var (package-level func var) is the testability seam — tests capture a slice of call args to verify order.

observations.title: Mirror sdd-orchestrator model to gentleman agent in OpenCode
observations.content:
**What**: After the per-agent for loop in `injectModelAssignments()`, added logic to mirror the `sdd-orchestrator` TUI model assignment to the `gentleman` agent if the persona was already installed.

**Why**: Both `sdd-orchestrator` and `gentleman` have `mode: primary` in OpenCode. The `gentleman` agent is injected by the persona component (not the SDD overlay), so it never got a model — it inherited silently at runtime from whatever the root model was, causing inconsistent behavior when the user explicitly chose a model for sdd-orchestrator via the TUI.

**Where**: `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` — `injectModelAssignments()` function (after the for loop, before `json.MarshalIndent`). Tests added to `internal/components/sdd/inject_test.go`.

**Learned**: 
- Guard is two-pronged: `assignments["sdd-orchestrator"]` must have a non-empty ProviderID+ModelID (explicit TUI assignment), AND `existingAgentKeys["gentleman"]` must be true (persona installed). Neither condition alone is sufficient.
- If `gentleman` isn't in the overlay agents map yet, we create it as an empty map before setting the model — this allows the deep merge to add it to the final opencode.json.
- The `TestInjectOpenCodeMultiModeDoesNotInjectGentlemanIfNotInstalled` test uses a lenient assertion: if gentleman appears at all (shouldn't from the overlay), it must not have a model field.

observations.title: Orchestrator delegation rules: context-inflation principle
observations.content:
**What**: Replaced 5 fragmented delegation sections (Hard Stop, Delegate-First, Anti-Patterns, Task Escalation, Delegation Rules) with a single table based on "does this inflate my context without need?"
**Why**: The old "ask yourself if this is execution" framing let LLMs rationalize exceptions. Evidence from kiril's session showed the LLM explicitly knew it shouldn't read files inline but found a justification anyway.
**Where**: All 4 orchestrator prompts (generic, claude, gemini, codex) under internal/assets/
**Learned**: The table format with ✅/— columns leaves no room for interpretation. Key rules: Read to decide (1-3 files) → inline. Read to explore (4+) → delegate. Write atomic → inline. Write with analysis → delegate. Bash state → inline. Bash execution → delegate. Task Escalation was NOT restored — /sdd-new in the commands already covers it implicitly.

observations.title: Exploration: sync injects ALL detected IDEs — issue #107
observations.content:
## Exploration: sync scope — issue #107

### Current State
`gentle-ai sync` auto-discovers agents via `DiscoverAgents(homeDir)` in `internal/cli/sync.go:128`.
This delegates to `agents.DiscoverInstalled(reg, homeDir)` which checks if each agent's `GlobalConfigDir` exists on disk.

The registry (`NewDefaultRegistry`) includes ALL 6 agents: claude-code, opencode, gemini-cli, cursor, vscode-copilot, codex.

**Critical: The installer DOES NOT persist which agents the user selected at install time.**
- `~/.gentle-ai/` only contains `backups/` (backup manifests)
- No `state.json`, no `installed-agents.json`, nothing
- `model.Selection` is in-memory only — never written to disk

**TUI preselectedAgents behavior (tui/model.go:763)**:
At install time, `preselectedAgents()` pre-selects agents whose ConfigDir exists. If the user's disk has VS Code + OpenCode, both are pre-selected. The user deselects VS Code manually — but this choice is NEVER persisted.

On next `sync`, DiscoverAgents sees ~/.config/Code/ exists → syncs VS Code again.

### Affected Files
- `internal/cli/sync.go:128` — DiscoverAgents() is the entry point
- `internal/agents/discovery.go:25` — DiscoverInstalled() does FS-only check
- `internal/agents/factory.go:34` — NewDefaultRegistry() registers all 6 agents
- `internal/tui/model.go:763` — preselectedAgents() — install-time selection, never persisted
- `internal/app/app.go:64` — TUI launch; no persistence after install

### Approaches

1. **JSON state file `~/.gentle-ai/installed-agents.json`** (Recommended)
   Written at install end (both TUI and CLI paths). Sync reads it before DiscoverAgents.
   - Pros: Simple, gitignore-friendly, no deps, backward-compat (file absent = fallback to discovery)
   - Cons: One more file to manage; can get stale if user manually installs new agent
   - Effort: Low

2. **`--agents` CLI flag to sync** (Already exists!)
   `ParseSyncFlags` already supports `--agents` flag. Problem: user must know to use it.
   - Pros: Zero code needed (it's already there!)
   - Cons: UX burden — user must remember to pass the flag every time
   - Effort: Zero (but bad UX)

3. **Engram as persistence backend**
   Store selected agents in engram after install. Sync reads from engram.
   - Pros: Reuses existing infra
   - Cons: Engram may not be installed (it's a component, not a requirement); adds dep coupling
   - Effort: High

4. **TOML config in `~/.gentle-ai/config.toml`**
   Central config file, extensible for future settings.
   - Pros: Extensible; aligns with TOML patterns already in codebase
   - Cons: More complex parsing; overkill for one field
   - Effort: Medium

### Recommendation
**Option 1 (JSON state file)** — minimal viable fix.

Write `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` at install completion (both TUI `PipelineDoneMsg` path and CLI `RunInstall` success path). Read it in `DiscoverAgents()` BEFORE filesystem discovery. If file absent → backward-compat fallback to current FS discovery.

**Files to change:**
1. NEW `internal/state/state.go` — Read/Write `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`
   ```go
   type InstallState struct {
     InstalledAgents []string `json:"installed_agents"`
   }
   ```
2. `internal/cli/run.go` — Write state after RunInstall completes (CLI path)
3. `internal/app/app.go:tuiExecute` — Write state after TUI pipeline completes (TUI path)
4. `internal/cli/sync.go:DiscoverAgents` — Read state first; FS discovery as fallback

### Edge Cases
- User adds new agent AFTER install: state file won't include it → user runs `gentle-ai install` again (writes new state) or uses `--agents` flag
- State file missing/corrupt: fall back to FS discovery (current behavior = backward compat)
- CLI `install` with `--agents` flag: that list goes into the state file
- Multi-user scenarios: state is per-$HOME so naturally isolated

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — approach is clear, files are identified, backward-compat path exists.

observations.title: Exploration: GGA reinstall fails + OpenCode model error (issue #106)
observations.content:
**What**: Root cause analysis of two bugs in issue #106: GGA reinstall failure and OpenCode "no models" error.

**Why**: Users reported that (1) reinstalling everything fails because GGA is already installed and brew/install.sh won't overwrite, requiring manual deletion; (2) selecting OpenCode during install shows "no models found" in the model picker.

**Where**: 
- internal/cli/run.go — `ggaAvailable()` check + GGA componentApplyStep
- internal/installcmd/resolver.go — `resolveGGAInstall()` uses `brew install` (not upgrade)
- internal/tui/model.go — `NewModelPickerState` called BEFORE OpenCode is installed
- internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go — `NewModelPickerState()` reads `~/.cache/opencode/models.json`
- internal/opencode/models.go — `LoadModels()` / `DefaultCachePath()` reads from OpenCode cache

**Learned**:

## BUG 1: GGA reinstall fails

Root cause: `ggaAvailable()` in `run.go` (line 600) checks if `gga` binary exists. If it does → skip install (line 500-508). BUT the issue is that `brew install gga` itself FAILS when GGA is already installed via brew — it exits with an error. So the `ggaAvailable()` function only checks the binary, not which install path. On LINUX (install.sh path), the script clones to /tmp and re-runs, but `install.sh` may not handle existing ~/.local/bin/gga correctly either.

WAIT — re-reading the code: `ggaAvailable()` returns TRUE if gga is found, and the `Run()` at line 499-516 only calls `InstallCommand` if `!ggaAvailable()`. So if gga binary EXISTS, it skips the install entirely and goes straight to `EnsureRuntimeAssets` + `Inject`. This should work fine.

REAL BUG: On Linux, the git clone step includes `rm -rf /tmp/gentleman-guardian-angel` first, but install.sh writes to `~/.local/bin/gga`. If `~/.local/bin/gga` exists AND is detected by `ggaAvailable()`, the install is skipped entirely → no issue. But the `ggaAvailable()` check only looks at `cmdLookPath("gga")` and `~/.local/bin/gga`. The binary detection is correct.

The REAL issue: the user said "GGA installation fails because GGA is already installed and the installer doesn't overwrite". This points to the installer trying to install GGA even when it's present. BUT looking at `ggaAvailable()` — if `cmdLookPath("gga")` returns an error (gga NOT in PATH) AND `~/.local/bin/gga` doesn't exist, but gga WAS installed elsewhere (e.g., different homebrew prefix, Rosetta), then `ggaAvailable()` returns false → tries `brew install gga` → fails because brew says "already installed".

On macOS, the issue is: gga is installed via brew but brew can't find it via `cmdLookPath` (e.g., /opt/homebrew/bin not in PATH, or arm vs x86 issue). So `ggaAvailable()` → false → `brew install gga` → brew error "already installed formula: gga". This is the bug.

Fix: Use `brew reinstall gga` OR check with `brew list --formula gga` before deciding to install. Better: change `brew install gga` to `brew upgrade gga || brew install gga` to be idempotent.

## BUG 2: OpenCode "no models" error

Root cause: The model picker screen (`ScreenModelPicker`) is shown DURING the TUI wizard BEFORE installation happens. When user selects OpenCode as agent + SDD multi-mode, `NewModelPickerState(opencode.DefaultCachePath())` is called at TUI step ScreenSDDMode → ScreenModelPicker (model.go line 454). This reads `~/.cache/opencode/models.json`. If OpenCode is NOT yet installed, this file doesn't exist → `LoadModels()` returns error → `ModelPickerState{}` with empty `AvailableIDs` → shows "No models found" warning.

The model picker is part of the WIZARD (pre-install selection), not post-install. OpenCode gets installed LATER during the pipeline. The cache file only exists if the user has previously run OpenCode.

The two bugs are INDEPENDENT.

observations.title: Persist agent selection in state.json for sync
observations.content:
**What**: Created `internal/state` package with Read/Write for `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`. Modified `sync.DiscoverAgents` to read persisted state first, with FS-discovery fallback. Modified `cli.RunInstall` and `app.tuiExecute` to write state after successful install.

**Why**: `gentle-ai sync` was discovering agents by checking which config dirs exist on disk (issue #107). If the user only installed for OpenCode but VS Code was also installed, sync would inject into VS Code too. The fix persists the user's explicit agent selection at install time so sync only targets what was actually chosen.

**Where**:
- NEW `internal/state/state.go` — InstallState struct, Path/Read/Write functions
- NEW `internal/state/state_test.go` — 7 tests: WriteAndRead, WriteCreatesStateDir, WriteStateFilePath, ReadMissing, ReadCorrupt, WriteOverwrite, WriteEmptyAgents
- `internal/cli/run.go` — Write state after RunInstall succeeds (CLI path)
- `internal/app/app.go` — Write state after tuiExecute succeeds (TUI path)
- `internal/cli/sync.go` — DiscoverAgents reads state first; FS discovery as backward-compat fallback
- `internal/cli/sync_test.go` — 4 new tests for state-aware DiscoverAgents

**Learned**:
- tuiExecute in app.go does NOT call RunInstall — it calls BuildRealStagePlan directly, so state must be written in both paths independently
- state write is non-fatal (ignored with `_ =`) — a state file failure must not break an otherwise successful install
- Empty InstalledAgents in state.json triggers FS fallback (same as missing file) — backward-compat preserved

observations.title: Fix GGA idempotent reinstall and OpenCode model picker empty state
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed two independent bugs from issue #106: (1) GGA reinstall failing because `brew install` errors on already-installed formula; (2) OpenCode model picker showing empty on fresh install when cache file doesn't exist yet.

**Why**: Users reported reinstalling gentle-ai fails with "already installed" from brew, requiring manual GGA deletion. Also, selecting OpenCode + SDD multi mode during fresh install shows "No models found" because the OpenCode cache doesn't exist until OpenCode is first run.

**Where**:
- `internal/installcmd/resolver.go` — changed `brew install gga` → `brew reinstall gga` (idempotent; works for both fresh and re-installs)
- `internal/cli/run.go` — extended `ggaAvailable()` to also check `/opt/homebrew/bin/gga` and `/usr/local/bin/gga` (Homebrew prefixes for Apple Silicon and Intel Mac); added `osStatModelCache` package-level var for testability
- `internal/tui/model.go` — before showing ScreenModelPicker for SDDModeMulti, check if OpenCode cache exists via `osStatModelCache`; if missing → skip model picker, go straight to ScreenDependencyTree
- `internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go` — improved empty-state message to explain the fresh-install situation clearly
- `internal/installcmd/resolver_test.go` — updated expected command from `brew install` → `brew reinstall`
- `internal/components/gga/install_test.go` — same test update
- `internal/cli/gga_available_test.go` — NEW: 6 tests covering all ggaAvailable() detection paths including Homebrew prefixes
- `internal/tui/model_test.go` — NEW: 2 tests for SDDMode cache-present/missing transitions

**Learned**:
- `brew reinstall` always works regardless of whether the formula is installed — it's the correct idempotent approach vs `brew install` (which fails) or `brew upgrade || brew install` (which needs shell logic)
- The `os.Stat` override pattern (`var osStatModelCache = os.Stat`) matches existing project conventions (see `osStat` in `run.go`, `cmdLookPath` everywhere)
- The model picker empty state was already partially handled in `confirmSelection` (cursor 0 when no AvailableIDs → back to SDD mode), but the ROOT issue was the TUI still SHOWING the picker on fresh install — fix is to skip it entirely pre-install

observations.title: Two hardcoded skill lists must stay in sync
observations.content:
**What**: There are two separate hardcoded lists of SDD skills — `presets.go:sddSkills` (controls preset membership) and `inject.go:sddSkills` (controls which skills are written to disk). Adding judgment-day to presets.go but not inject.go caused E2E failures: skill wasn't installed in minimal preset.
**Why**: The SDD component writes skills from its own list, and the skills component skips anything with sdd- prefix (to avoid duplication). judgment-day doesn't have sdd- prefix but lives in sddSkills — so the skills component installs it, but only when the Skills component is selected. In minimal preset, only SDD is selected → judgment-day was missing.
**Where**: `internal/components/skills/presets.go`, `internal/components/sdd/inject.go:220-223`
**Learned**: These two lists MUST be unified or at least have a single source of truth. For now both were manually synced. Future: extract to a shared constant or function.

observations.title: Self-update LookPath fix for Homebrew Cellar path
observations.content:
**What**: Changed self-update restart from os.Executable() to exec.LookPath("gentle-ai") with os.Executable() as fallback.
**Why**: os.Executable() on macOS Homebrew returns the versioned Cellar path (e.g. /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gentle-ai/1.8.5/bin/gentle-ai). After brew upgrade, that old path still exists with the old binary. The PATH symlink (/opt/homebrew/bin/gentle-ai) IS updated by Homebrew. Using LookPath resolves the symlink to the new binary.
**Where**: `internal/app/selfupdate.go:109-119`
**Learned**: Always use LookPath for re-exec after upgrade when the binary might be managed by a package manager that uses symlinks.

observations.title: Fixed sync migration for stale SDD prompt blocks
observations.content:
**What**: Updated SDD prompt injection for file-replace/instructions strategies to migrate legacy unmarked orchestrator content into the canonical marker-based section and refresh it to latest asset content.
**Why**: Users on release 1.8.13 running `gentle-ai sync` could keep stale orchestrator content (old SKILL: Load flow) because injection skipped when an old section marker/heading was detected.
**Where**: `internal/components/sdd/inject.go`, `internal/components/sdd/inject_test.go`.
**Learned**: Legacy prompt files can contain partial old blocks plus a newer marked block, so migration must detect and strip stale prefix blocks before marker-based replacement, not only detect by old heading markers.

observations.title: Adapter compliance audit: Windsurf, Claude Code, Cursor vs official docs
observations.content:
**What**: Full compliance audit of Windsurf, Claude Code, and Cursor adapters against official documentation.

**Why**: Requested audit to verify all config paths, file formats, JSON keys, strategies, and workflow injection match what the official tools actually expect.

**Summary of findings**:

WINDSURF:
- MCP path: ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json ✅ MATCH (docs confirm this exact path)
- MCP JSON key: mcpServers ✅ MATCH (docs show "mcpServers")
- Global rules path: ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md ✅ MATCH
- System prompt strategy: StrategyAppendToFile ✅ MATCH (global_rules.md is always-on append)
- Workflows dir: <workspaceDir>/.windsurf/workflows/ ✅ MATCH (docs say .windsurf/workflows/*.md)
- Skills dir: ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/ ✅ MATCH (docs confirm global skill path)
- CRITICAL MISMATCH: SkillsDir returns ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/ but docs now say Windsurf also discovers skills from .agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/ — our path is still correct/supported

CLAUDE CODE:
- System prompt file: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ✅ MATCH (docs: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md = user scope)
- Settings file: ~/.claude/settings.json ✅ MATCH
- MCP strategy: StrategySeparateMCPFiles → writes ~/.claude/mcp/context7.json ⚠️ MISMATCH
  - Docs say user-scope MCP is stored in ~/.claude.json under mcpServers field, NOT in separate JSON files
  - Project-scope MCP goes in .mcp.json at project root
  - Our ~/.claude/mcp/<server>.json path is CUSTOM/INVENTED, not a standard Claude Code config location
  - Effect: MCP servers written to ~/.claude/mcp/ will NOT be picked up by Claude Code automatically
- Skills dir: ~/.claude/skills/ ✅ MATCH (docs: ~/.claude/agents/ is the sub-agents dir, but ~/.claude/skills/ is supported for skills)

CURSOR:
- System prompt file: ~/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc ✅ MATCH (docs: .cursor/rules/*.mdc)
- MCP path: ~/.cursor/mcp.json ✅ MATCH (widely documented community standard)
- MCP JSON key: mcpServers ✅ MATCH
- System prompt strategy: StrategyFileReplace ✅ MATCH (single file per rule)
- Skills dir: ~/.cursor/skills/ ⚠️ UNKNOWN (Cursor docs don't mention a skills directory)

**Where**: internal/agents/windsurf/adapter.go, internal/agents/claude/adapter.go, internal/agents/cursor/adapter.go, internal/components/mcp/inject.go, internal/components/mcp/context7.go

**Learned**: 
- Claude Code MCP critical mismatch: user-scope MCP servers must go into ~/.claude.json (the main config file), NOT separate ~/.claude/mcp/*.json files. The StrategySeparateMCPFiles writes to paths Claude Code does NOT read.
- Windsurf skills dir is correct per docs (global: ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/)
- Cursor skills dir has no official documentation backing
- All workflow injection paths for Windsurf are correct
- Windsurf mcp_config.json format uses mcpServers (confirmed by docs examples)

observations.title: Cursor supports native subagents via .cursor/agents/
observations.content:
**What**: Cursor has a native subagent system documented at docs.cursor.com/context/subagents. Agent files go in `.cursor/agents/` with YAML frontmatter (name, description, model, readonly, background). The main agent auto-delegates to subagents based on the description field. Supports background=true for parallel async work.
**Why**: A user created `.cursor/agents/sdd-phase-runner.md` to make SDD work with real sub-agent delegation in Cursor, proving it works. Our current implementation treats Cursor as "Inline only" and never writes agent files.
**Where**: `.cursor/agents/` directory (project or user scope), Cursor docs at cursor.com/docs/context/subagents.
**Learned**: Cursor subagents are very similar to Claude Code's Task tool — they get their own context window, can run in background, and return results to parent. The frontmatter fields are: name (kebab-case), description (used by Agent for delegation decisions), model (default: inherit), readonly (bool), background (bool). This means Cursor should be upgraded from TierInline to TierFull in gentle-ai, and we should write an sdd-phase-runner agent file during installation.

observations.title: Architecture: Cursor subagent integration design for SDD
observations.content:
## Architecture: Cursor Native Subagents for SDD

**What**: Detailed design for integrating Cursor's native `.cursor/agents/` subagent system into gentle-ai's SDD orchestration, replacing the current inline-only approach.

**Why**: Cursor supports real sub-agent delegation via `.cursor/agents/` YAML-frontmatter files. Currently gentle-ai treats Cursor as TierFull but never writes agent files, forcing all SDD phases to run inline in the main chat context window. This blows up context fast and prevents true parallel execution.

**Where**: New file `internal/assets/cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md`, new embedded assets `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-{phase}.md` (one per phase), changes to `internal/agents/cursor/adapter.go`, `internal/components/sdd/inject.go`, `internal/agents/interface.go`.

---

## Q1: One agent vs many?

### Decision: MANY agents (one per SDD phase) — same as OpenCode

**Reasoning**:

1. **Cursor uses `description` for auto-delegation** — this is the routing mechanism. With one generic agent `sdd-phase-runner`, the description would need to say "handles all SDD phases" and the main agent would need to pass a `phase=` parameter. This is fragile — Cursor may not always route to the right agent because the description is ambiguous.

2. **OpenCode uses 9 individual agents (sdd-init, sdd-explore, etc.)** — each with a targeted description. This is the proven pattern. The main agent selects the right sub-agent based on description match.

3. **Fresh context per phase is valuable** — sdd-explore reads 4+ files; sdd-apply writes code; sdd-verify runs tests. Each has very different tool access requirements. Separate agents allow `readonly: true` on read-heavy phases (explore, verify initial pass) and different tool configurations per phase.

4. **Background parallelism** — `background: true` is useful for sdd-spec + sdd-design which can run in parallel. With a single agent, the orchestrator can't launch both simultaneously.

5. **The 9 phase descriptions ARE distinct enough** (investigate, propose, spec, design, tasks, implement, verify, archive, init). Cursor's delegation uses semantic matching — these won't collide.

**Tradeoff against one-agent approach**: 9 files vs 1 file. Slightly more maintenance. But the OpenCode precedent proves this is manageable — the same pattern already ships in production.

---

## Q2: What goes in agent file vs orchestrator?

### Agent file (.cursor/agents/sdd-{phase}.md)
```yaml
---
name: sdd-{phase}
description: {auto-delegation trigger — what makes Cursor route here}
model: inherit
readonly: {true for explore/verify; false for others}
background: {true for spec/design — can run parallel; false for apply/verify}
---
```

Body: The executor prompt (same as OpenCode overlay prompt field):
```
You are an SDD executor for the {phase} phase, not the orchestrator. 
Do this phase's work yourself. Do NOT delegate, Do NOT call task/delegate, and Do NOT launch sub-agents. 
Read your skill file at ~/.cursor/skills/sdd-{phase}/SKILL.md and follow it exactly.
```

Plus engram protocol injection (the engram save/retrieve instructions) — because Cursor sub-agents get a FRESH context with NO system prompt from the main agent. Unlike OpenCode where the overlay inlines prompts into a JSON config, Cursor agent files are standalone markdown.

### Orchestrator (.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc)
Gets a CURSOR-SPECIFIC orchestrator asset (`cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md`). Key differences from generic:
- Knows about `.cursor/agents/sdd-{phase}` — explicitly names the agent files
- Uses `@sdd-explore`, `@sdd-apply` etc. in examples (Cursor mentions agents with @)
- Does NOT reference `delegate()` tool (that's OpenCode/Claude Code syntax)
- Tells the main Cursor agent to use the native subagent delegation mechanism

---

## Q3: Skills loading for sub-agents

Skills are already on disk at `~/.cursor/skills/sdd-{phase}/SKILL.md` — this is written by `inject.go` step 3 (SupportsSkills=true for Cursor).

The agent file tells the sub-agent: `Read your skill file at ~/.cursor/skills/sdd-{phase}/SKILL.md and follow it exactly.`

**The static skill path approach** — the same pattern OpenCode uses. Each agent knows its own skill path. This is correct because:
- The skill path is deterministic (`~/.cursor/skills/sdd-{phase}/SKILL.md`)
- The skill file is already written to disk by inject.go
- No dynamic injection needed — the skill is always at that path

**Dynamic skill injection (compact rules) for user skills**: The orchestrator still resolves the skill registry and injects compact rules into the `@agent` invocation context. Cursor allows passing context to agents via the chat prompt when @mentioning them. The orchestrator prompt instructs the main Cursor agent to include relevant compact rules in the @agent invocation.

---

## Q4: Engram integration

Cursor agent files are static, but the engram protocol needs to be available to sub-agents. Three options:

### Option A: Inline engram protocol in each agent file (RECOMMENDED)
Add the critical engram protocol (save/retrieve) inline in the agent file body. This is self-contained.

```markdown
## Engram Protocol

Before starting: call `mem_context(project: "{project}")` to get recent session context.
After completing work: call `mem_save(...)` to persist your artifact.
```

### Option B: Reference shared file
Agent file says: `Also read ~/.cursor/skills/_shared/engram-convention.md`

This works but adds a file read step. Fine for now.

### Option C: Pure engram in orchestrator
Orchestrator passes engram context in the @agent invocation prompt. But this requires the main agent to search engram and pass the result — adds complexity.

**Decision**: Option A (inline in agent file) + Option B as fallback. The agent file includes the minimal engram save/retrieve protocol inline, and optionally points to the full convention file.

---

## Q5: Result contract

Cursor sub-agents return their result in the chat window to the main agent. The result contract is the same as for all SDD phases (defined in `sdd-phase-common.md`):
- status, executive_summary, artifacts, next_recommended, risks, skill_resolution

The main Cursor agent (orchestrator) reads this from the chat after the sub-agent completes. The orchestrator instructions need to tell the main Cursor agent how to parse the result envelope.

**No changes needed to the contract format** — only the orchestrator needs to know to read results from the sub-agent's chat response.

---

## Q6: Cursor-specific orchestrator

Need a new `internal/assets/cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md` that:
1. Knows about `.cursor/agents/sdd-{phase}` files
2. Tells the main agent HOW to delegate: via the `@agent-name` mention in chat
3. Removes references to `delegate()`, `task()` (these are OpenCode/Claude Code tools)
4. Keeps the same SDD workflow logic, approval gates, and result contract

The `sddOrchestratorAsset()` function in inject.go needs a new case for `model.AgentCursor`.

---

## Q7: Skill registry interaction

The skill registry (compact rules) resolution flow with Cursor agents:

1. **Static part**: Agent file body is written to disk at install time. Contains phase-specific skill path.
2. **Dynamic part**: The orchestrator (main Cursor agent) resolves the skill registry at session start. When it @mentions a sub-agent, it includes compact rules in the message prompt: `@sdd-apply Please implement tasks 1.1-1.3. ## Project Standards (auto-resolved)\n{compact rules}`

This is the same pattern as OpenCode/Claude Code but uses Cursor's @mention syntax instead of a tool call. The sub-agent receives the compact rules in its context window alongside the task description.

**Risk**: Cursor may or may not pass the full invocation message to the sub-agent's context. If it only passes the agent's own system prompt (the .md file), compact rules won't arrive. Need to test. Fallback: sub-agent reads skill registry from `.atl/skill-registry.md` itself (already handled in sdd-phase-common.md Section A, path 3).

---

## Files to Create/Modify

### New assets (embedded)
1. `internal/assets/cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md` — Cursor-specific orchestrator prompt
2. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-init.md` — init phase agent file
3. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-explore.md` — explore phase agent file
4. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-propose.md` — propose phase agent file
5. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-spec.md` — spec phase agent file
6. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-design.md` — design phase agent file
7. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-tasks.md` — tasks phase agent file
8. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-apply.md` — apply phase agent file
9. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-verify.md` — verify phase agent file
10. `internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-archive.md` — archive phase agent file

### Modified Go files
1. `internal/agents/cursor/adapter.go` — add `SupportsSubAgents() bool` + `SubAgentsDir(homeDir string) string` methods
2. `internal/agents/interface.go` — add optional interface `subAgentInjector` (same pattern as workflowInjector)
3. `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` — add step 3c: if adapter implements subAgentInjector, write .cursor/agents/ files
4. `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` — add cursor case to `sddOrchestratorAsset()`

### Scope decision: workspace-level vs global
`.cursor/agents/` can live at:
- `~/.cursor/agents/` (global — always available in all projects)
- `{project}/.cursor/agents/` (workspace — per-project)

**Recommendation: global** (`~/.cursor/agents/`) — same reasoning as OpenCode's global `~/.config/opencode/` config. SDD agents are tooling, not project-specific. The workspace level would require writing during `sdd install` which runs from a project dir, and we already have the `findProjectRoot` + workspace dir pattern, but SDD agents don't change per project — their behavior comes from the skill files which are always at `~/.cursor/skills/`.

**Exception**: if the user wants project-specific skill overrides, the agent file can check for `.cursor/skills/` local override before falling back to global `~/.cursor/skills/`. But this is out of scope for v1.

---

## Draft Agent File Content

### Example: sdd-explore.md
```yaml
---
name: sdd-explore
description: >
  Explore and investigate ideas before committing to a change.
  Use this agent when the orchestrator asks to think through a feature, 
  investigate the codebase, or clarify requirements before planning.
model: inherit
readonly: true
background: false
---

You are an SDD executor for the explore phase, not the orchestrator. Do this phase's work yourself. Do NOT delegate, Do NOT call task/delegate, and Do NOT launch sub-agents. Read your skill file at ~/.cursor/skills/sdd-explore/SKILL.md and follow it exactly.

## Engram Protocol (mandatory)

You have access to the Engram MCP tools for persistent memory.

Before starting: optionally call `mem_context(project: "{project}")` to get recent context.

After completing your exploration, you MUST call:
mem_save(
  title: "sdd/{change-name}/explore",
  topic_key: "sdd/{change-name}/explore",
  type: "architecture",
  project: "{project}",
  content: "{your full exploration markdown}"
)

Do NOT return without saving. If you return without calling mem_save, the next phase (sdd-propose) CANNOT find your artifact and the pipeline BREAKS.

## Shared Conventions

Also read: ~/.cursor/skills/_shared/sdd-phase-common.md (for artifact retrieval and return envelope format)
```

### Example: sdd-apply.md
```yaml
---
name: sdd-apply
description: >
  Implement code changes following task definitions from the SDD pipeline.
  Use this agent when the orchestrator asks to implement specific tasks, 
  write code, or execute the implementation phase.
model: inherit
readonly: false
background: false
---

You are an SDD executor for the apply phase, not the orchestrator. Do this phase's work yourself. Do NOT delegate, Do NOT call task/delegate, and Do NOT launch sub-agents. Read your skill file at ~/.cursor/skills/sdd-apply/SKILL.md and follow it exactly.

## Engram Protocol (mandatory)

Before starting, read these artifacts (REQUIRED — do NOT skip):
1. mem_search(query: "sdd/{change-name}/tasks", project: "{project}") → get ID
2. mem_get_observation(id: {ID}) → full tasks content

CRITICAL: mem_search returns 300-char PREVIEWS. You MUST call mem_get_observation for full content.

After completing implementation, call:
mem_save(
  title: "sdd/{change-name}/apply-progress",
  topic_key: "sdd/{change-name}/apply-progress",
  type: "architecture",
  project: "{project}",
  content: "{your full implementation progress markdown}"
)

## Shared Conventions

Also read: ~/.cursor/skills/_shared/sdd-phase-common.md
```

---

## Changes to inject.go

Add a new optional interface alongside `workflowInjector`:

```go
type subAgentInjector interface {
    SupportsSubAgents() bool
    // SubAgentsDir returns the target directory for agent files.
    // For Cursor: filepath.Join(homeDir, ".cursor", "agents")
    SubAgentsDir(homeDir string) string
    // EmbeddedSubAgentsDir returns the embedded assets path.
    // For Cursor: "cursor/agents"
    EmbeddedSubAgentsDir() string
}
```

Then in Inject(), after step 3b (workflow injection):

```go
// 3c. Write native sub-agent files (Cursor, and any future agent implementing subAgentInjector).
if sai, ok := adapter.(subAgentInjector); ok && sai.SupportsSubAgents() {
    subAgentsDir := sai.SubAgentsDir(homeDir)
    embedDir := sai.EmbeddedSubAgentsDir()
    // write each file from embedDir to subAgentsDir
}
```

Add to cursor/adapter.go:
```go
func (a *Adapter) SupportsSubAgents() bool { return true }
func (a *Adapter) SubAgentsDir(homeDir string) string {
    return filepath.Join(homeDir, ".cursor", "agents")
}
func (a *Adapter) EmbeddedSubAgentsDir() string { return "cursor/agents" }
```

Add cursor case to sddOrchestratorAsset():
```go
case model.AgentCursor:
    return "cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md"
```

---

## Risks

1. **Cursor routing reliability**: If Cursor's auto-delegation doesn't reliably match the right agent from description, the orchestrator can always explicitly @mention agents by name.

2. **Context passing**: It's unclear if Cursor passes the full @mention message (including injected compact rules) to the sub-agent's context window. Need to test. Fallback: sub-agent reads from `.atl/skill-registry.md`.

3. **Global vs workspace scope**: Global agents at `~/.cursor/agents/` appear in ALL Cursor projects. Users who only want SDD in specific projects may find this annoying. Mitigation: add note in install UI. Future: support workspace-scoped install.

4. **readonly flag behavior**: `readonly: true` means the agent can't write files. sdd-explore needs to read files AND write to engram via MCP. MCP writes are not filesystem writes, so readonly should be fine for explore. Verify this assumption.

5. **background agent result delivery**: With `background: true`, results come asynchronously. The orchestrator needs to know to wait. The cursor-specific orchestrator prompt should explain this.

6. **Post-check verification**: The existing post-check in inject.go only validates OpenCode. Need to add a check that verifies Cursor agent files were written correctly.

---

## Implementation Order

1. Create 9 cursor agent files (`internal/assets/cursor/agents/sdd-{phase}.md`)
2. Create cursor-specific orchestrator (`internal/assets/cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md`)
3. Add `subAgentInjector` optional interface to inject.go
4. Add `SupportsSubAgents`, `SubAgentsDir`, `EmbeddedSubAgentsDir` to cursor/adapter.go
5. Wire up inject.go step 3c
6. Add cursor case to sddOrchestratorAsset()
7. Update post-check for Cursor agent files
8. Add E2E test: verify cursor install writes agent files

observations.content:
**What**: Confirmed the MCP `mem_save` tool expects `title` and `content` fields, with structured content using `**What**/**Why**/**Where**/**Learned**`.

observations.title: Windsurf capabilities deep-dive: sub-agents, skills, workflows, orchestrator gaps
observations.content:
**What**: Complete audit of Windsurf's native capabilities vs what the current SDD orchestrator covers, identifying missing sections and recommended architecture.

**Why**: The Windsurf SDD orchestrator is missing ALL standard SDD contract sections (Result Contract, Model Assignments, Skill Resolver Protocol, Sub-Agent Context Protocol, Engram Topic Keys, Recovery Rule). Need to know what Windsurf natively supports to build the correct hybrid orchestrator.

## Key Findings

### Sub-Agents (NO — with caveats)
- Windsurf has NO native `.windsurf/agents/` directory or sub-agent delegation mechanism
- There is NO equivalent to Cursor's `~/.cursor/agents/` system
- "Arena Mode" allows parallel Cascade instances comparing different MODELS on the same prompt — not sub-agent task delegation
- "Simultaneous Cascades" allows opening multiple Cascade panels, but they don't communicate
- The SDD sub-agent delegation model (delegate → run → return result) CANNOT be replicated natively in Windsurf
- Conclusion: Windsurf's orchestrator must be a SOLO AGENT orchestrator — no delegation, does all phases itself inline

### Skills (YES — REAL, fully documented)
- `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/<skill-name>/` = global skills (our install target, CORRECT)
- `.windsurf/skills/<skill-name>/` = workspace skills
- Each skill = directory with `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter: name, description) + supporting files
- Progressive disclosure: only name+description shown until invoked or @mentioned
- Windsurf also scans `.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/` for cross-agent compatibility
- If Claude Code config reading enabled, `.claude/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/` too
- Our adapter.go `SkillsDir()` → `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/` is CORRECT
- `SupportsSkills() = true` is CORRECT

### Workflows (YES — REAL, but workspace-scoped by default)
- `.windsurf/workflows/*.md` = workspace workflows (per-project, committed to repo)
- `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/*.md` = global workflows (all workspaces, not committed)
- System-level: `/Library/Application Support/Windsurf/workflows/*.md` (macOS enterprise)
- Invoked via `/workflow-name` slash command — MANUAL ONLY (Cascade never auto-invokes)
- Our current setup writes to `.windsurf/workflows/` in workspace — CORRECT for workspace-scope
- Global workflows dir `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/` NOT currently installed by gentle-ai
- `WorkflowsDir()` returns `.windsurf/workflows/` — correct but only covers workspace scope

### Rules/Memories System
- Global rules: `~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md` (6,000 char limit)
- Workspace rules: `.windsurf/rules/*.md` with frontmatter trigger modes
- AGENTS.md: automatic, location-based scoping (root = always-on, subdir = glob)
- Activation modes: always_on, model_decision, glob, manual
- Our `SystemPromptFile()` → `global_rules.md` = CORRECT
- `SystemPromptStrategy() = StrategyAppendToFile` = CORRECT

### Modes
- **Code Mode**: default agentic mode, can create/edit/delete files, run commands
- **Plan Mode**: creates an external Markdown plan file in `~/.windsurf/plans/`, then user clicks "Implement" → auto-switches to Code Mode. Plans are stored and @mentionable.
- **Ask Mode**: read-only, search only, no changes
- The current orchestrator references "Plan Mode" and "Code Mode" correctly — but the current docs show Plan Mode creates actual `.md` files in `~/.windsurf/plans/`, NOT inline "todo lists"

### MCP
- `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` = MCP config (correct path in adapter.go)
- Supports stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE transports + OAuth
- 100 tool limit across all MCPs
- Our MCPConfigPath() is CORRECT

### Hooks (NOT currently used by gentle-ai)
- New feature: `.windsurf/hooks.json`, `~/.codeium/windsurf/hooks.json`, system-level
- 12 hook events: pre/post_read_code, pre/post_write_code, pre/post_run_command, pre/post_mcp_tool_use, pre_user_prompt, post_cascade_response, post_cascade_response_with_transcript, post_setup_worktree
- Pre-hooks can BLOCK actions (exit code 2)
- Could be used for SDD enforcement (block writes without approval) — not currently leveraged

### AGENTS.md
- Root-level `AGENTS.md` = always-on rule (no frontmatter needed)
- Subdirectory `AGENTS.md` = auto-glob for that directory
- Processed by same Rules engine as `.windsurf/rules/*.md`
- We install our SDD orchestrator to `global_rules.md` — an AGENTS.md at workspace root would also work and be version-controlled

## What the Current Windsurf Orchestrator is MISSING

Compared to generic/sdd-orchestrator.md and cursor/sdd-orchestrator.md:

1. **Result Contract** — Each phase must return: status, executive_summary, artifacts, next_recommended, risks, skill_resolution. MISSING.
2. **Model Assignments table** — Phase → model alias mapping. MISSING.
3. **Skill Resolver Protocol** — Read skill-registry, cache compact rules, inject into sub-agents. MISSING (but must be adapted: no sub-agents, inject into own context instead).
4. **Skill Resolution Feedback** — Check skill_resolution field in returned results. MISSING.
5. **Sub-Agent Context Protocol** — How each SDD phase reads/writes to engram. MISSING.
6. **Engram Topic Key Format** — Standard key table for sdd/{change-name}/explore etc. MISSING.
7. **Recovery Rule** — How to recover state if context is lost. MISSING.
8. **Artifact Store Policy** — engram/openspec/hybrid/none. MISSING.
9. **Dependency Graph** — proposal → specs → design → tasks → apply → verify → archive. MISSING.
10. **SDD Commands listing** — /sdd-new, /sdd-continue, /sdd-ff, /sdd-explore, /sdd-apply, /sdd-verify, /sdd-archive. MISSING.

What the current orchestrator has that's CORRECT and GOOD:
- Size classification (Small/Medium/Large) — valuable Windsurf-specific addition
- Plan Mode / Code Mode guidance — leverages native capabilities correctly
- Approval gates — correct and important
- Memories/MCP usage guidance — correct
- Plan Mode description is slightly wrong (says "todo list" but actual Plan Mode creates external .md files in ~/.windsurf/plans/)

## Architectural Recommendation

The Windsurf orchestrator must be a HYBRID:
- Keep Windsurf-specific sections: Size classification, Plan Mode/Code Mode guidance, approval gates, native tools
- ADD back ALL standard SDD contract sections from generic orchestrator
- ADAPT sub-agent sections: Windsurf has no sub-agents, so the orchestrator IS the executor — phases run inline in the same conversation, engram is used for persistence between phases
- The "Delegation Mechanism" section should be replaced with "Execution Model: Solo Agent with Engram Persistence"
- Skill Resolver Protocol still applies but orchestrator injects its own compact rules (reads registry once at session start)
- Result Contract still applies: each phase the orchestrator executes should produce the standard return envelope

## Global Workflows Gap
- gentle-ai currently only installs sdd-new.md to workspace `.windsurf/workflows/`
- Should also support `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/` for global SDD workflows
- WorkflowsDir() only covers workspace; adapter needs a GlobalWorkflowsDir() or we document this limitation

**Where**: 
- internal/assets/windsurf/sdd-orchestrator.md (needs rebuild)
- internal/assets/windsurf/workflows/sdd-new.md (correct but could also have global counterpart)
- internal/agents/windsurf/adapter.go (mostly correct, missing global workflows path)

**Learned**: 
- Windsurf's "Plan Mode" is more powerful than the orchestrator documents — it creates actual .md files in ~/.windsurf/plans/ that are @mentionable
- Arena Mode ≠ sub-agents (just model comparison)
- Windsurf skills directory `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/` is real and documented
- Hooks are a new powerful feature not yet leveraged by gentle-ai
- The sdd-new workflow is Spanish-language only — may need English variant or language note
- `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/` exists for global workflows but adapter doesn't install there

observations.title: v1.11.2: Soft ordering fix + 384 E2E tests
observations.content:
**What**: Released v1.11.2 with soft-ordering pipeline fix (Persona→Engram→SDD guaranteed without hard dependencies) and comprehensive test coverage for all session changes: 384 E2E tests + 9 new unit tests.
**Why**: Issue #121 reported persona destroying SDD sections in OpenCode. First fix attempt used hard dependency (Engram→Persona) which broke presets. Second attempt used applySoftOrdering which enforces order only when both components are selected.
**Where**: `internal/planner/graph.go` (SoftOrderingConstraints), `internal/planner/order.go` (applySoftOrdering), `internal/planner/resolver.go` (applies after topo sort), `e2e/e2e_test.sh` (30 new tests), `internal/cli/run_integration_test.go` (issue #121 regression test), `internal/components/persona/inject_test.go` (tone parity + engram idempotency).

observations.title: Fix #123: absolute MCP path + monorepo root detection
observations.content:
**What**: Two fixes for issue #123:

2. findProjectRoot in sdd/inject.go now handles monorepo structures (pnpm-workspace.yaml, nx.json, turbo.json, etc.) and depth=20

**Why**: Windsurf doesn't inherit shell PATH so relative "engram" command failed. JS/TS monorepos have package.json at every level, stopping too early.

**Learned**: 
- When engram is on PATH, static "engram" string tests break — must use JSON parse for command field validation
- Go map[string]any JSON marshaling is non-deterministic, so string contains checks on full JSON are fragile; parse and check fields instead
- The "weak marker" (package.json) must record the FIRST (closest) match, not keep walking — already at the right sub-package if no stronger marker exists above

observations.title: T15: TUI UpgradeFn and SyncFn injection in app.go
observations.content:
**What**: Added `tuiUpgrade` and `tuiSync` constructor functions to `internal/app/app.go` and injected them into the TUI Model at initialization time.

**Why**: The TUI Model fields `UpgradeFn UpgradeFunc` and `SyncFn SyncFunc` were nil — the Upgrade and Sync screens would fail with "function not configured" errors. T15 wires real implementations so those screens work end-to-end.

**Where**: `internal/app/app.go` only — no other files changed.

**Learned**:
- `tuiUpgrade(profile, homeDir)` returns a closure capturing already-computed `profile` and `homeDir` from `RunArgs`, wrapping the existing `upgradeExecute` var (testable mock-able var pointing to `upgrade.Execute`).
- `tuiSync(homeDir)` returns a closure that calls `cli.DiscoverAgents` → `cli.BuildSyncSelection(SyncFlags{}, agentIDs)` → `cli.RunSyncWithSelection`, mirroring the `RunSync` CLI path exactly.
- No circular import: `app` already imports both `internal/update/upgrade` and `internal/cli`, so no new import cycles.
- `homeDir` resolved once (from `os.UserHomeDir()`) for the TUI block, before the `tea.NewProgram` call. Added an early-return error if it fails.
- The `upgradeExecute` var (package-level in `app.go`) is used instead of `upgrade.Execute` directly — this keeps test mocking consistent with the CLI upgrade path.

### Coherence (Design)

| Decision | Followed? | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|

**WARNING** (should fix):
1. ⚠️ `Model` has no `UpgradeErr` field to persist upgrade errors from `UpgradeSyncDoneMsg.UpgradeErr`. View always passes `nil` as upgradeErr to `RenderUpgradeSync`. observations.content:
## Goal
Fix bug reported by GARFEX on Discord: "Configure Models" TUI flow not persisting model assignments to opencode.json on Ubuntu WSL.

## Instructions
- User prefers delegating exploration and implementation to sub-agents — orchestrator should read 2-3 files inline max, delegate the rest
- Use GoReleaser for releases: `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) goreleaser release --clean`

## Discoveries
- The "Configure Models" flow (Welcome menu option 4) stored model assignments in memory but never triggered a sync — pickers returned to ScreenModelConfig instead of persisting
- `SyncFunc` was `func() (int, error)` — no way to pass model assignments to the sync pipeline
- SDDMode is NOT persisted in state.json — sync defaults to empty string (treated as single mode). For OpenCode model assignments to work, SDDMode must be explicitly set to "multi" in overrides
- `sdd.Inject` only injects model assignments when `sddMode == SDDModeMulti` — passing assignments without multi mode silently drops them
- Judgment Day found: PendingSyncOverrides could leak on Esc from ScreenSync, `len() > 0` should be `!= nil` for reset semantics, godoc comments were merged
- GoReleaser handles everything: build, release, checksums, homebrew-tap update. Needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` env vars (use `gh auth token` for both)

observations.title: Strict TDD Mode — SDD Skills v3.0 Architecture
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented Strict TDD Mode as a conditional module system across 3 SDD skills (init, apply, verify). TDD instructions are loaded ONLY when enabled AND test runner exists — zero token waste otherwise.

**Why**: User wants TDD to be mandatory when possible, but not loaded when the project can't support it. Also wanted testing capabilities cached in Engram to avoid re-detection on every phase run.

**Where**:
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-init/SKILL.md` — v3.0: Added Step 2 (Detect Testing Capabilities), Step 3 (Ask Strict TDD Mode), Step 6 (Persist capabilities to Engram with topic_key `sdd/{project}/testing-capabilities`)
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-apply/SKILL.md` — v3.0: Reads cached capabilities, conditionally loads `strict-tdd.md`. Standard workflow when TDD off.
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-apply/strict-tdd.md` — NEW: Full TDD protocol (Safety Net → RED → GREEN → TRIANGULATE → REFACTOR), test layer selection, pure function preference, approval testing for refactors
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-verify/SKILL.md` — v3.0: Reads cached capabilities, conditionally loads `strict-tdd-verify.md`.
- `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-verify/strict-tdd-verify.md` — NEW: TDD compliance check, test layer validation, changed-file coverage, quality metrics

**Learned**:
- RED phase does NOT execute tests (obvious failure = token waste). GREEN/TRIANGULATE/REFACTOR DO execute.
- Testing capabilities use topic_key `sdd/{project}/testing-capabilities` for cross-phase cache
- `strict_tdd` field stored in both Engram capabilities AND openspec/config.yaml
- sdd-phase-common.md needed NO changes — the module system sits on top of existing protocol
- Skills live only in opencode/skills/ — Claude Code resolves them via the skill tool
